deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

domain_name.description: Relative name of the domain serving the application. Example: example.com.
domain_name.rationale: The relative domain name served by the mapping (e.g. example.com). This is an identifier/name; we do not constrain resource names and a generic policy cannot pin a team-specific domain.

override_strategy.description:
Whether the domain creation should override any existing mappings for this domain.
By default, overrides are rejected. Default value: "STRICT" Possible values: ["STRICT", "OVERRIDE"]
override_strategy.rationale: to enforce a clear resolution strategy for domain mapping conflicts to prevent accidental hijacking of custom domains from other projects and ensure predictable routing behavior.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: It is a standard provider-inherited field as the resource is inherently constrained by the project-level permissions and deployment context of the authenticated service account.

ssl_settings.description: SSL configuration for this domain. If unconfigured, this domain will not serve with SSL.

ssl_settings.certificate_id.description:
ID of the AuthorizedCertificate resource configuring SSL for the application. Clearing this field will
remove SSL support.
By default, a managed certificate is automatically created for every domain mapping. To omit SSL support
or to configure SSL manually, specify 'SslManagementType.MANUAL' on a 'CREATE' or 'UPDATE' request. You must be
authorized to administer the 'AuthorizedCertificate' resource to manually map it to a DomainMapping resource.
Example: 12345.
ssl_settings.certificate_id.rationale: Identifier referencing an existing AuthorizedCertificate resource for the domain mapping. We do not constrain references to other resources, so it is not a policy target.

ssl_settings.ssl_management_type.description:
SSL management type for this domain. If 'AUTOMATIC', a managed certificate is automatically provisioned.
If 'MANUAL', 'certificateId' must be manually specified in order to configure SSL for this domain. Possible values: ["AUTOMATIC", "MANUAL"]
ssl_settings.ssl_management_type.rationale: Mandates 'AUTOMATIC' SSL management to utilise Google's managed certificate authority, ensuring renewals and the use of modern cryptographic protocols without human intervention.
